answer: Pay for a unique completed job, not for participation. A client escrows one fixed fee and publishes a verifier plus a deadline. Workers commit result hashes; after the deadline, the first valid commitment to reveal a passing result gets that fee, and every other claim gets zero. The atlas assigns each job one spent marker, so an ocean of aliases cannot collect twice for the same output. A ledge of extra keys buys no bonus: a farm must finish additional independently funded jobs to earn additional fees.
